No unique scenic or esthetic resources exist within the Long Spur Ridge site that could not be found in the proposed Bad Creek site, and in the other alternative sites as well as in any of the numerous adjacent valleys. On a scale from 0 to 10, with higher number values representing greater esthetic attributes, the Long Spur Ridge site has been rated 5, compared with a rating of 3, 7, and 7 given to the proposed Bad Creek site, the Bearcamp Creek site, and the Coley Creek site, respectively (Dysart et al., 1973).
Impacts on scenic and esthetic resources resulting from construction of this proposed alternative would drastically change the landscape, the degree of change depending on the size and character of project lake and appurtenant facilities.
8.3.1.5 Recreation
The Long Spur Ridge alternative would inundate a 3.4 mile reach of Thompson River, one of the major streams in the region. However, slightly less combined land-water area providing recreational opportunities would be inudated than at the proposed Bad Creek site. Fishing appears to be the most significant outdoor recreation activity that now occurs within the Long Spur Ridge site. The area is accessible from Bohaynee Road, which extends northeast to southwest, a short distance north of the reservoir site. A trail parallels the Thompson River in this area and is reported to receive heavy use by fishermen. On a scale from 0 to 10, with higher number values representing greater recreational attributes, the Long Spur Ridge site has been rated as 5 and the Bad Creek site as 4. The recreation ratings of the sites were formulated by H. Jesse Grove (Dysart, et al., 1973) on the basis of field observations. The ratings reflect a variety of general factors such as (a) ease of accessibility, (b) land area with topographic suitability for user facilities development, (c) size and quality of existing stream resource, (d) degree of vegetative disruption evident, and (e) level of present public use.
Reservoir-oriented outdoor recreation facilities would not be developed at this alternative site due to weekly 130-foot fluctuations in surface elevation of the reservoir. Off-site recreation development would be required.
